answer: Embodied Latency Attestation Challenge. Each identity must return a hardware-signed timing trace of a physical challenge-response loop through a device the operator owns, with round-trip bounds tight enough that remote relays fail. The ivory seal on each trace binds it to one device serial. Attackers cannot fake timing across a horizon of distributed proxies without violating the latency window, so each identity costs a distinct physical unit plus its maintenance, not a cheap key. A fable of shared devices collapses when serials collide.
